title: The Brightest Cosmic Explosion Ever Recorded
description: Discover GRB 221009A, the brightest gamma-ray burst in cosmic history, which shook Earth's upper atmosphere from over two billion light-years away.

beats.text: An explosion two billion light-years away physically rattled Earth's upper atmosphere.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a massive star collapse and black hole formation

beats.text: On October 9, 2022, a massive star located 2.4 billion light-years away in the constellation Sagitta violently collapsed directly into a black hole.
beats.visual: starfield image of the constellation Sagitta, 2022

beats.text: The resulting gamma-ray burst was quickly dubbed the BOAT by astronomers, standing for Brightest Of All Time.
beats.visual: Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope illustration, NASA
queries: Fermi Gamma ray Space Telescope illustration

beats.text: It completely shattered previous space records by being roughly seventy times brighter than any prior gamma-ray burst ever recorded.
beats.visual: Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer satellite illustration, NASA
queries: Swift Gamma Ray Burst Explorer satellite

beats.text: That blinding cosmic flash was so overwhelmingly intense that it temporarily saturated and blinded most space telescope detectors.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope model in space, NASA

beats.text: Specialized lightning detectors in India and Germany confirmed Earth's ionosphere was perturbed, as the blast disrupted longwave radio communications.
beats.visual: Earth upper atmosphere glow and ionosphere, NASA
